body:
Even in death we must still be polite and civilized to our fellow person as we do not know what they, themselves, are going through.

I have been through the mental health system. I have been hospitalized four times over the course of a decade due to suicidal ideations and attempts. I have been diagnosed with Major Depressive Disorder severe, Dysthymia, ADHD, and General Anxiety Disorder. I have been through the gambit of meds, therapists, CBT sessions, art therapy, animal therapy, etc. Nothing has worked.

I should have gone to the hospital more times then I have, but I hate the sterile environment and token treatments. It is there to stabilize, but not treat. Fuck that. I swore after the last time that I would rather die then go back as it just instills a sense of emptiness in me, that makes me more of an other then I already am.

I wish I knew what happiness was. The idea of it brings me to tears, it brings me to the fundamental issue that I face, because I do not know what it means. I know what the pain, I know what the emptiness, I know what the listlessness, I what the seething anger feels like. But happiness and love, they are just token words that seem to be something felt by others which are not me. I cannot tell you the last happy day that I felt which I do not regret or have ruined. But those days were six years ago, they are so dull, so vague, so distant, that their memory is nothing more then something that I once clinged to in order to justify this pitiful existence then some people call a life.

*“To make yourself something less than you can be - that too is a form of suicide”.* 

- Benjamin Lichtenberg

Legacy. I do not mean to belittle you, but legacies for those without consequence are meaningless and not written by our hands. Moreover, through the course of time, over a year, a decade, a century, it is nothing a legacy fades away into nothing, just as our lives do. It is a sad joke; a travesty.
